comment: License allow/deny policy enforced by scripts/license-gate.mjs and (on PRs) actions/dependency-review-action. See docs/LICENSE_POLICY.md.
comment_denied: Strong copyleft / source-available licenses that must never enter the resolved tree without an explicit, reviewed exception agreed by the maintainers.
comment_exceptions: Weak-copyleft / non-OSI licenses already present in the resolved tree. Each entry is an explicit, reviewed acceptance, not a blanket allowance; the gate stays silent on these exact strings only.

exceptions.reason: Test-only accessibility checker (axe-core) reached through Playwright/a11y tooling. Weak file-level copyleft: we do not modify or redistribute source files, and it is not present in production images. Accepted 2026-10-02.

Sharp's Windows-only prebuilt native binary (optional platform dependency, pulled via the sharp override). Not loaded on Linux production images; LGPL obligations attach to the binary, which we do not modify or bundle. Accepted 2026-10-02; revisit if sharp is used on Windows in a distributed artifact.

Sentry CLI, a build/CI/observability tooling dependency, not linked into or redistributed with the product. FSL is source-available (not OSI) and converts to MIT after its change date. Accepted 2026-10-02; re-evaluate if Sentry CLI becomes part of a shipped artifact.

browser-assert@1.2.1 declares NO license field at all in its published package.json (verified by reading the installed package), so it is reported as UNKNOWN rather than as a denied license. It is a dev-only transitive dependency of Storybook (@storybook/core, @storybook/builder-webpack5), never present in production images or shipped artifacts. Its repository (socialally/browser-assert) carries no LICENSE file. Accepted 2026-10-02 as a packaging omission, not a policy claim; replace or vendor it if Storybook drops it, and re-check if it ever enters a production path.
